witness.description: For each n in 1..30, p_n = least prime congruent 1 mod n; witness records p_n. Verifier recomputes p_n by exact integer arithmetic and checks p_n is prime, p_n ≡ 1 (mod n), and no smaller number ≡ 1 (mod n) is prime — establishing the definition of p_n and the congruence n | (p_n - 1) for n = 1..30.

run.detail: TypeError: verify() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given

claim: RESULT == True establishes the finite fragment of L1: for every n in 1..30 the least prime p_n ≡ 1 (mod n) is exactly the recorded value, hence n | (p_n - 1) and phi(p_n) = p_n - 1 ≡ 0 (mod n), certifying the definitional reduction behind m_n <= p_n's witness congruence on n <= 30 by exact integer arithmetic, with no imports, no filesystem, no network, fail-closed by boolean return.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
